title: netwatch diagnose run --format json, schema 2
description: One bounded diagnosis. Later minors may add fields, so ignore any you do not know. A break needs netwatch 2.0 and a new schema file. A field marked deprecated tells you nothing useful, so do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version. A finding with beta true comes from a rule with no reviewed contract: its shape follows this schema, but the rule can change thresholds or disappear. Exit 3, for bad arguments or a session that could not start, prints no JSON at all. This file describes what netwatch 0.40 and later write; 0.39 has no metadata block.

metadata.description: Names this output's schema. Every stable netwatch output has this block, at the same path.

netwatch_version.description: The netwatch that wrote this document.

version.description: The netwatch version, the same as metadata.netwatch_version. Not a schema version.

ruleset.description: How many rules this build's catalogue holds. A count that grows between releases, not a version.

outcome.description: Closed set: a new value needs netwatch 2.0, because each one is an exit status. no_finding means the run had evidence and no Issue counted towards the exit status. It is not a health claim: a rule that could not be evaluated did not fire, and issues can still list a beta rule's Issue, which counts only with --include-beta. finding means at least one Issue counted. incomplete means no usable observation arrived and no Issue counted, and it can list a beta rule's Issue too. Retry it with a longer budget, and do not read it as health.

exit.description: The process's exit status: 0 for no_finding, 1 for finding, 2 for incomplete. Closed set: a new value needs netwatch 2.0.

include_beta.description: Whether --include-beta was given. Without it a beta rule's issue is listed but does not set the exit status.

target.description: The --target name. Null for a run about the host.

started_at.description: RFC 3339 with this host's UTC offset. Finding timestamps have no offset, so read it from here.

window_seconds.description: How long the run sampled, in seconds, which can have a fraction. A different thing from window_secs on a finding's evidence.

evidence.description: Whether the run saw a usable observation of what it was asked about.

completeness.description: What the outcome can be taken to mean, in words. The wording is not stable.

coverage.description: Which rules had their inputs on this host.

reason.description: In words, unlike doctor's reason code. The wording is not stable.

issues.description: Faults. Only an Issue from a contracted rule, or any Issue with --include-beta, sets the exit status.

severity.description: Closed set: see the finding's severity.

observations.description: Things worth knowing that are not faults. They never set the exit status.

local_time.description: Local wall-clock time on the host, with no UTC offset. This is not UTC, so do not parse it as UTC. started_at in the same document has the host's offset.

rule_id.description: A rule in the catalogue. An existing id keeps its meaning. Open set: a minor may add a rule, so ignore an id you do not know.

availability.description: Why a rule input or a check has something or nothing to say. Open set: a minor may add a word, so treat an unknown value like unknown, which older recordings can also carry.

kind.description: Derived from severity: info is an observation, anything else an issue. Closed set: a new value needs netwatch 2.0.

id.description: Unique within this run's engine, not across runs or hosts.

severity.description: Closed set: a new value needs netwatch 2.0, because severity decides kind and with it the exit status.

title.description: In words. The wording is not stable; use rule for matching.

stale_since.description: From when this finding's evidence stopped arriving. Absent, not null, while it is arriving.

beta.description: Opened by a rule with no reviewed contract.

state.description: An object, so the value is at state.state. A check's state is a plain string. Schema 2 keeps this shape.
A run lists only open findings, so this is open. acked is the other value a session can give one. Open set: treat an unknown value as open, because the finding is listed.

metric.description: A dotted metric name such as dns.rtt_p50.

unit.description: A display suffix such as ms or %, which can be empty.

baseline.description: The learned baseline, when one exists.

sigma.description: The baseline's standard deviation. Present exactly when baseline is.

window_secs.description: Seconds of data the value summarises, as an integer. A different thing from the top-level window_seconds, which is how long the run sampled.

configuration.description: An opaque revision of a configured target. Absent for other subjects.

via_iface.description: The interface this finding's traffic used. Absent when not known.

via_resolver.description: The resolver this finding's lookups used. Absent when not known.

processes_measured.description: Absent means false. true with empty processes means attribution was tried and named nobody, which is not the same as every process.

note.description: A qualifier in words, such as service, not network. The wording is not stable.

id.description: Stable within its rule. Match on this, not on label.

label.description: In words, and built at run time for some causes. The wording is not stable.

id.description: Stable within its cause. Match on this, not on name.

name.description: In words. The wording is not stable.

state.description: Closed set: a new value needs netwatch 2.0. not_run is not a failure and does not count against the cause.

why_not.description: Why the check did not run. Present exactly when state is not_run.

detail.description: In words. The wording is not stable.

weight.description: Relative importance within the cause. 2 or more marks the check that tells this cause from its lookalikes.

text.description: In words. The wording is not stable.

detail.description: In words, or the literal command. The wording is not stable.

kind.description: instruct is something for the operator to run, escalate is something to send to someone. apply belongs to the TUI. Open set: treat an unknown value as instruct.

key.description: The TUI hotkey. A run applies nothing, and keybindings can change in any release. Do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version.

action.description: What the TUI would do for an apply step. A run applies nothing. Do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version.

reversible.description: Whether the TUI could undo an apply step. A run applies nothing. Do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version.

requires.description: The privilege an apply step needs in the TUI. A run applies nothing. Open set: a minor may add a privilege. Do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version.

applied.description: What became of an apply step in the TUI. Always null from a run. Do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version.

verify.description: The condition that would close this finding in a session.

predicate.description: Closed set: a new value needs netwatch 2.0, because the threshold means nothing without it.

consequences.description: The ids of findings this one hides as consequences of the same cause. Those findings are not listed in this output.

recurrence.description: Times this finding reopened inside the recurrence window.

artifacts.description: Files a session's report attached. Always empty from a run. Do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version.

suppressed_by.description: The finding hiding this one. Always null from a run, which lists only findings nothing hides. Do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version.

tests.description: Discriminating tests run from the TUI. Always empty from a run. Do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version.

verification.description: Whether a step the user carried out in the TUI worked. Always null from a run. Do not rely on it. It goes only in a major version.

subject.description: What the finding is about. Each kind has its own fields, listed together here and required by kind below.

kind.description: Open set: a minor may add a kind, so treat an unknown one as the host and read the finding's rule.
